lease_g.source: Aircraft-lease-rental revenue growth on FY2025's 219.8 — the leased-out fleet (17 aircraft to JV airlines) grows with Abu Dhabi's ~40% capacity expansion, Fly Jinnah, Egypt at the raised 49%, and the Saudi DMM launch

jet_eff_base.source: EFFECTIVE (hedge-blended) jet fuel price path, USD/bbl — the study's CENTRAL CONTESTED JUDGEMENT, priced BOTH ways (see jet_eff_alt). BASE = the EIA-curve framing: 2025 market average ~USD 89/bbl (IATA); H1-2026 spiked (IATA monitor USD 158.77 early Aug-2026) but the book is partly hedged 2026-2028 (Note 24 swaps/collars; RATIOS undisclosed — flagged) and Q1-2026's realised margin shows nothing like a spot-price hit; EIA July-2026 STEO Brent 81.91 (2026) -> 64.76 (2027) then a mild crack-normalised drift. Fuel cost per passenger = intensity x this path — its own commodity escalator, never a CPI proxy

jet_eff_alt.source: The ALTERNATIVE fuel framing: IATA's June-2026 high-fuel view persists through the hedge blend — no EIA-style relief. Published side by side with the base everywhere the base appears

fuel_intensity.source: Fuel intensity, AED per passenger per USD/bbl of effective jet price: FY2025 audited fuel cost/pax 172.4 (Note 29 / presentations) over the ~USD 89/bbl 2025 market average (IATA) = 1.937. Held flat — the neo's ~20% lower burn is an upside not credited

fleet_cons.source: CONSOLIDATED fleet block (Sharjah + Ras Al Khaimah): YE2025 = 56 aircraft per the company's own FY2025 presentation fleet allocation (Sharjah 54, RAK 2; the 90 total is GROUP-wide incl. the JV hubs). Forward: 16 net additions to ~72 by FY2030 (within the 120-aircraft order and Airbus's constrained output), split ~7 owned / ~9 leased at ~AED 184mn owned cost (~USD 50mn A320neo family net) and ~AED 175mn right-of-use inception value per leased aircraft; owned units loan-financed ~AED 150mn each (FY2025 actual: AED 849.6mn for 5 = 170/unit). The owned/leased split remains UNDISCLOSED — flagged and sensitised

maint_per_pax.source: Maintenance cost per passenger, AED, +4%/yr on FY2025's 61.3 (FY2023: 43.4 — the step-up is the ageing ceo fleet plus sector-wide MRO inflation; neos relieve it only gradually). Its own MRO escalator

ga_g.source: Cash G&A growth (FY2025 cash G&A = 316.3 less 40.1 depreciation = 276.2) — scale plus wage drift

sm_pct.source: S&M held at FY2025's 1.46% of revenue (FY2024: 1.53%)

dna_path.source: Depreciation and amortisation, AED mn, FY26E-FY30E — grows with the OWNED fleet: FY2025's 621.8 steps up as loan-financed neo deliveries (5 in FY2025, ~3-4/yr assumed owned henceforth) enter the depreciable base; leased deliveries enter ROU depreciation similarly. Fleet-driven, not a revenue ratio

capex_path.source: Fleet capex including pre-delivery payments, AED mn. FY2025 actual: 2,327.6 (a catch-up year: 5 owned aircraft + PDP build). Forward: ~3-4 owned aircraft/yr at ~AED 185mn each plus a continuing PDP ladder on the 120-aircraft order; leased deliveries (the majority) do NOT pass through capex (additions to lease liabilities: 472.2 FY2025, 538.9 FY2024). The owned/leased delivery split is NOT disclosed — FLAGGED as the build's weakest driver and sensitised heavily

nwc_pct.source: Operating working capital as a share of revenue, held at the historical band: (inventories + current receivables) less (current payables + deferred income + maintenance provisions + staff benefits) = -65.3% (FY23), -62.2% (FY24), -66.6% (FY25) of revenue. An airline sells tickets before it flies and accrues maintenance/end-of-service liabilities — growth RELEASES cash. -64% is the three-year centre, not the best year

assoc_g.source: Share-of-JV/associate-profit growth path on FY2025's 189.975: FY2026 held near-flat (the JV hubs absorbed the same H1 disruption; Air Arabia DMM start-up costs begin), then +18/+18/+15/+12% as Abu Dhabi (+40% capacity plan), Fly Jinnah, Egypt (49%) and DMM ramp. The 100%-basis FY2025 P&Ls (Note 12) grew 77% (Abu Dhabi) and 80% (Jinnah) y/y

other_g.source: Other-income growth on FY2025's 197.1 (management fees from the JV network 86.9 + misc) — fee income scales with JV activity

dep_rate_path.source: Yield on cash + fixed deposits: FY2025 disclosed average 4.41% (Note 17), rolled down with the CBUAE base-rate path (3.65% held 29-Jul-2026, Fed flat-to-easing bias)

payout.source: Dividend payout on attributable profit: FY2025's AED 0.30/share = 86% of EPS 0.35, DPS raised 5 fils every year since FY2022 (0.15/0.20/0.25/0.30). FY2026 held at 0.30 (100% of a dip-year EPS, funded by net cash), then ~85-90%

rf.source: AED sovereign anchor: UAE Ministry of Finance dirham T-Bond auction, July-2026 — January-2031 tranche YTM 4.48% (4bp over comparable UST; May-2026 auction: 4.30%). The LOCAL-currency government bond, per the standing rule, not a USD proxy

sov_spread_obs.source: The OBSERVED default spread embedded in the AED sovereign yield actually used: the July-2026 MoF auction priced the January-2031 tranche 4bp over comparable US Treasuries (May-2026: 14bp). Netting THIS spread — not the 42bp rating-table spread — keeps the risk-free rate currency-consistent under the 1:1 peg (UST 5-yr 4.35% on 07-Aug-2026, US Treasury daily curve): 4.48% - 0.04% = 4.44% > 4.35%. Adopted after external critique; the rating-basis netting (4.06%) is published as the alternative construction

sov_spread_rating.source: Damodaran adjusted default spread, United Arab Emirates row (Moody's Aa2), original ctryprem file last updated 5-Jan-2026. Netted out of the local yield so sovereign risk is not double-counted

erp_rating.source: Damodaran total equity risk premium, UAE row, rating basis (mature 4.23% + CRP 0.64%), 5-Jan-2026 file. The CDS column for the UAE is NA in the same file, so the rating basis is the ONLY published construction — both-bases publication is therefore rating + a stated NA, not two numbers

erp_cds.source: UAE sovereign CDS column: NA in Damodaran's January-2026 file — no CDS-basis ERP exists to publish; stated plainly rather than substituted

beta_used.source: Tier-1 OWN-STOCK regression: AIRARABIA weekly log-returns vs the DFM General Index (DFMGI), 5-year window to 16-Jul-2026: beta 1.086, R-squared 0.402, n=258, SE 0.083, CI90 [0.95, 1.22] — clears the usability gate, not weak-instrument flagged. See beta_result.json

kd_booked_path.source: BOOKED blended finance-cost rate on the rolling gross debt book: FY2025 effective 2.73% (finance costs 66.7 / average gross debt), rising as new leases (~4%, Note 25) and new aircraft loans (~marginal 5.4%) replace older cheaper layers

debt_amort.source: Scheduled repayments of borrowings + lease principal (FY2025 actuals: 393.7 borrowings repaid + 248.1 lease principal ≈ 642 gross; forward net of refinancing ~500-580/yr)

kd.source: Marginal AED cost of debt: the AED sovereign 4.48% (Jan-2031) plus ~100bp unsecured corporate allowance for an unrated but NET-CASH flag carrier affiliate. Evidence table: FY2025 lease book carries an average 4% finance charge (Note 25, SECURED on aircraft — a floor, not the marginal unsecured rate); the FY2025 aircraft loan was similarly secured; deposits EARN 4.41%. 5.5% sits above the sovereign, above the secured book, and above the deposit rate, as it must

kd_path.source: Forward marginal Kd, easing ~50bp with the Fed/CBUAE path over five years — the discount-rate glide takes its shape from this path by construction

kd_term.source: Terminal AED cost of debt: long-run UAE sovereign norm ~4.0% + 100bp corporate spread

rf_term.source: Terminal risk-free rate, norm-built: ~2% UAE/US long-run inflation (CBUAE projects 1.8-2.0%) + ~2pp real — the mature-market neutral-rate convention for a hard-pegged currency. Never a historical average, never backed out of a price

erp_term.source: Terminal equity risk premium: between the mature-market 4.23% and today's UAE 4.87% — the Aa2 country premium is small and kept

wd_term.source: Terminal debt weight D/(D+E) on a GROSS basis, ~today's 10.2% gross weight held: the airline runs structurally net-cash but carries secured aircraft debt and IFRS-16 leases permanently

g_term.source: Terminal growth 2.5%, AED-nominal against a 4.0% terminal risk-free that embeds ~2% inflation — about 0.5pp real, for a carrier whose home market (Sharjah 19.5mn airport pax +13.9% in 2025) is still structurally growing. Sensitised 1.5-3.5%

ev_ebitda_just.source: Justified EV/EBITDA on mid-cycle FY2027E EBITDA EXCLUDING the fee/other-income stream (valued separately — basis matched to how peer multiples are computed). Peer set rebuilt from PRIMARY filings after external critique: Ryanair 6.50x (FY26 EBITDA EUR 3,747.6mn = op profit 2,374.2 + dep 1,373.4; 1,039.2mn shares and EUR 2.7bn net cash per the Q1-FY27 report), Wizz ~4.75x (FY26 EBITDA 1,318.3), easyJet ~3.5x, IndiGo 11.1x, Pegasus ~6.6x (EUR-functional IFRS) -> median 6.5x. Bear 5.0x / bull 8.0x

pe_just.source: Justified through-cycle P/E on normalised earnings. Peers: Ryanair 12.6x, easyJet 12.4x, Jazeera ~17.7x computed, Damodaran profitable-airlines 12.87x. 13x reflects a structurally profitable LCC with net cash and a growing equity-accounted network. Bear 10x / bull 16x

roe_sust.source: Sustainable return on equity for the book lens. Trailing ROE on average attributable equity: 19.9% (FY2025), 18.9% (FY2024) — struck slightly below the record year

jv_pe.source: Capitalisation multiple for the JV/associate airline network in the ALTERNATIVE bridge framing: the share of profit (189.975, growing double-digit) at 15x — a growth-LCC multiple in line with Jazeera and above the mature peers. The BASE framing carries the audited carrying value 363.386 instead. THE CONTESTED JUDGEMENT, published both ways, never averaged

nci_book.source: Non-controlling interests at audited carrying value, 31-Dec-2025 — the correct deduction basis (the prior profit-share-ratio proxy deducted 2.9)

lens_weights.source: DCF primary for an operating airline with a disclosed unit history; relative and normalised secondary; book least — an airline's book equity understates a slot/brand/JV franchise

anchor_days.source: Days from the DCF construction date (31-Dec-2025, the audited balance-sheet date) to the anchor 7-Aug-2026. All lens values are rolled to the anchor at the cost of equity, net of the AED 0.30 FY2025 dividend paid inside the window

subnames.leasing: Aircraft leases to the JV network

egypt.note: stake raised from 40% to 49% during FY2025

dmm.note: Air Arabia DMM LLC, Saudi JV established FY2025 — pre-operational

e3.method_short: cash returns vs cost of capital

assert_log: AIRARABIA — ASSERT / derivation log (built on the audited FY22-25 + Q1-2026 filings)

[Historical income statement] every FY2023-25 line is the audited/restated figure. Operating profit closes to the audited statement in all three years (FY25: 1,269.6 = revenue 7,787.6 - direct 6,088.1 - G&A 316.3 - S&M 113.6). House EBITDA (operating profit + D&A): FY23 1,886, FY24 1,833, FY25 1,891 (24.3% of revenue); including the recurring other-income line (management fees from the JV network) FY25 2,089. Effective tax: FY24 8.79%, FY25 11.60% — the forecast provides at the statutory 15% DMTT.

[Unit economics, disclosed] FY2025 on 13.06mn consolidated passengers: fare+baggage 478.7/pax (FY24 494.9), ancillary 64.8 (60.4), fuel 172.4 (171.5), staff 81.9, maintenance 61.3, landing 36.0, handling 29.4. Load factor 85.3% (record). Seat/ASK data is not disclosed: passengers x per-pax rates is the finest sourced level, and the gap is flagged rather than reconstructed.

[Working capital, audited] operating WC (inventories + current receivables less payables, deferred income, maintenance provisions and staff benefits): FY23 -3,918 (-65.3% of revenue), FY24 -4,208 (-62.2%), FY25 -5,187 (-66.6%) — deeply NEGATIVE: tickets are sold before they are flown and maintenance/end-of-service obligations accrue ahead of cash. Growth releases cash.

[Net debt] gross borrowings + lease liabilities: FY23 2,279, FY24 2,101, FY25 2,781; cash + fixed deposits 5,246 / 5,320 / 5,199 -> NET CASH of 2,417 at FY2025 (3,218 FY2024). The bridge quantity is interest-bearing debt less cash and deposits; deferred income and provisions live in working capital, never double-counted.

[Kd integrity] (i) the audited book is SECURED and cheap: leases at an average 4% finance charge (Note 25), the FY2025 aircraft loan mortgage-secured; effective finance cost / average gross debt = 2.73%. (ii) the adopted MARGINAL Kd 5.50% deliberately sits ABOVE the secured effective rate and ABOVE the AED sovereign 4.48% — a same-currency corporate cannot fund below its sovereign unsecured. (iii) deposits earn 4.41%: the marginal Kd also clears the opportunity yield on the asset side.

[Cost of equity] AED sovereign 4.48% (MoF T-Bond auction Jul-2026, Jan-2031 tranche) less the OBSERVED 4bp spread the auction itself priced over US Treasuries = rf* 4.44% — currency-consistent under the peg (UST 5-yr 4.35% on 07-Aug-2026); the rating-basis netting (4.06%) is published as the alternative. + beta 1.086 (own-stock weekly vs DFMGI, R2 0.40) x ERP 4.87% (Damodaran UAE row, Jan-2026; CDS column NA — stated, not substituted) -> Ke 9.73%.

[WACC explicit] GROSS-debt weights 10.2%/89.8% -> 9.21%. On the NET basis the company is net cash (weight -11.0%), which would push the rate to 10.28%; the gross basis is used because the bridge separately credits the cash pile at face value, and the gross basis is the conservative (lower-discount-rate-on-nothing) choice here: it is the LOWER of the two, matched by adding cash in the bridge rather than pretending the discount rate is higher.
[WACC terminal] Ke 9.16% (rf 4.00% + beta x ERP 4.75%); Kd after tax 4.25%; weights 90%/10% -> 8.67%
[Glide] forward WACC 9.21% -> 8.94% -> 8.80% -> 8.67% -> 8.67%; discount factors 0.9156, 0.8405, 0.7725, 0.7109, 0.6542. The glide fractions are the cost-of-debt path's own cumulative progress.
[Margins are OUTPUTS] EBITDA margin 21.1% -> 24.3% -> 23.4% -> 22.7% -> 21.9% (FY2025 actual 24.3%). The FY2026 compression is the fuel spike + flat traffic; FY2027 recovers on the EIA fuel path.
[FY2026 cross-check against the print] Q1-2026 revenue 1,800.4 grossed up on Q1-2025's seasonal share of FY2025 implies 7,880; the build produces 7,869 (-0.1%).

[Leased-fleet charge — adopted from external critique] the forecast leased aircraft (9 of the 16 consolidated additions) are no longer acquired for free: their gross right-of-use inception value (175, 350, 350, 350, 350) is charged inside FCFF as leased capex — the 'firm buys all capacity with capital' convention, with the financing mix left to the WACC. The NPV-0-financing alternative (strip leased assets from invested capital, charge nothing) is worth ~+0.09/share and is noted, not adopted.

[FCFF waterfall] NOPAT (on EBIT including the recurring fee/other-income line, at the 15% DMTT) 982, 1,255, 1,291, 1,341, 1,377; capex 2,000, 1,900, 1,900, 1,950, 2,000; working-capital release -151, +373, +516, +536, +549 -> FCFF -624, 187, 457, 557, 635.

[Forecast net finance — rebuilt after critique] gross debt now ROLLS with the financing of the fleet (leases + aircraft loans - amortisation): 2,606 -> 2,586 -> 2,546 -> 2,636 -> 2,706; finance costs at the booked blended rate 84, 86, 90, 93, 99 (no hardcoded factor); finance income 213, 118, 70, 34, 4. BOTH financing legs are tax-effected in the net-debt roll; the JV/associate share sits BELOW the tax line (equity-method income arrives net of the ventures' own tax). Attributable profit 1,286, 1,511, 1,544, 1,600, 1,643; EPS 0.276, 0.324, 0.331, 0.343, 0.352; DPS floored at 30 fils throughout — the dividend ladder holds in the base case by construction, funded by net cash in the dip year.
[Invested capital] FY2025: fleet assets (PP&E + right-of-use + pre-delivery payments) 8,671 + intangibles 1,362 + working capital -5,187 = 4,847; ROIC 25.7%. Terminal ROIC (NOPAT(n+1)/IC(n)) 14.3%.

[Terminal value] reinvestment g/ROIC = 17.5%; terminal NOPAT 1,411; TV 18,876 at terminal WACC 8.67% minus g 2.5%, discounted at the year-5 factor 0.6542 -> PV 12,348. Terminal value is 94% of operating enterprise value — HIGH, because the explicit window carries the fleet build-out's capex while its revenue tail sits beyond FY2030; said plainly, not hidden.

[JV network — BOTH WAYS, never averaged] BASE: audited carrying value 363. ALTERNATIVE: capitalised share of FY2025 profit 190 x 15 = 2,850. The gap (+0.53/share) is the single most consequential contested judgement in this study: five airline JVs (Abu Dhabi, Egypt at a raised 49%, Fly Jinnah, Maroc, the pre-operational Saudi DMM) whose combined 100%-basis profits grew ~65% in FY2025 sit on the balance sheet at less than 2.0x their annual profit share.

[Bridge] operating EV 13,099 + NET CASH 2,417 + non-operating assets (FVOCI investments 458 + investment property 277 + net investment in lease 335) + JV network at carrying value 363 = 16,949; less minorities (0.02%) 1 -> equity 16,948 = AED 3.63/share at 31-Dec-2025; rolled 219/365 at Ke (x1.0573) less the AED 0.30 dividend paid in the window = AED 3.51 vs spot 5.24 (-33%) — the operating equity rolls at Ke, the cash/near-cash legs at the deposit yield, and minorities are deducted at their audited carrying value. ON THE ALTERNATIVE JV FRAMING: AED 4.06 (-23%).

[Fuel framing both ways] BASE (EIA July-2026 STEO path, relief in 2027): AED 3.51. ALTERNATIVE (IATA June-2026 high-fuel assumption held): AED 1.86 — -1.66/share. Both published; the workbook carries the base and the alternative side by side.
[DCF scenarios] bear 0.47 / base 3.51 / bull 7.23 (the bull adopts the JV-capitalised framing; the bear the IATA fuel path)

[Relative lens — basis-matched after critique] 6.5x FY2027E EBITDA EXCLUDING fees/other income (2,056) — the same basis peer multiples are computed on — plus the fee stream valued separately as an after-tax annuity (3,169), discounted and bridged -> AED 3.60/share. Trailing prints for context, BOTH bases: EV/EBITDA 11.7x ex-fees / 10.6x incl-fees; P/E 15.0x. Peer set rebuilt from primary filings: Ryanair 6.50x, Wizz 4.75x, easyJet 3.5x, IndiGo 11.1x, Pegasus 6.6x -> median 6.5x.

[Normalised lens — de-JV'd] mid-cycle EBITDA margin 23.4% (FY2028E) on FY2026E revenue 7,869 + fees/other + net finance income, EXCLUDING the JV share -> normalised EPS 0.267 x 13 plus the JV network at BOOK (AED 0.08/share) = AED 3.45/share. The base-framing central now genuinely carries the JV at carrying value in every lens.
[Book lens] justified P/B 2.33x = (18% - 2.5%) / (9.16% - 2.5%) on BVPS 1.80 -> AED 4.13/share. Trailing ROE 19.9%.

[Range — weighted after critique] the published bear/bull are now weighted the same way as the base: 1.81 - 5.66; the widest single-lens span (0.47 - 7.23, the DCF scenarios) is shown separately and labelled as such.
[Synthesis] weighted central AED 3.61; full span 0.47 - 7.23; spot 5.24 (-31% to the central). On the JV-capitalised framing the central becomes 3.86 (-26%) — both stated, never averaged.
[Expert panel] Expert 1 4.13 [3.11-5.15]; Expert 2 2.08 [1.45-2.75]; Expert 3 3.46 [2.67-4.01]; panel median 3.46 (-34% vs spot)
[Catalyst quantity, defined] one quarter's deferral of the FY2027 fuel relief = (fuel/pax FY26 - FY27) x FY27 passengers x (1-t) / 4 / shares = AED 0.019 per share per quarter.
